name: Silkpeel

lead: SilkPeel is a diamond-tip dermabrasion facial. A provider glides a fine diamond-surfaced wand over the skin to remove the top layer of dead cells.
People use it to improve texture, dullness, fine lines and mild pigmentation, usually as a series of sessions.

paras: The abrasive tip, often paired with suction, gently removes the outermost skin layer, revealing smoother skin and helping products penetrate better.
Side effects are usually mild and temporary: dryness, sun sensitivity, occasional bruising. Results fade, so sessions are repeated every few weeks.

web.title: Hyaluronic acid serums with diamond tip microdermabrasion (2023)

chain: Diamond-tip wand removes the outer dead layer of skin
angle.text: The treatment polishes away the dull outer layer of skin so the face looks smoother and brighter right after a session, and it can help skincare products absorb better. Results fade, so people repeat sessions every few weeks.

lead: SilkPeel is a branded diamond-tip dermabrasion treatment, a gentle exfoliating facial performed in a clinic or medspa. People use it to smooth rough texture, brighten dull skin and soften fine lines and mild sun damage so the complexion looks fresher and more even.[1]

Diamond-tip systems use a roughened wand with fine diamond particles bonded to the surface instead of the aluminum oxide crystals of older microdermabrasion machines. Because no crystals are blown into the air, they are considered easier to use near the eyes and lips, and diamond tips date to 1999.[1] Treatments are typically repeated every two to four weeks, since results from this lighter class of exfoliation are temporary.[1]

Published studies of diamond-tip microdermabrasion are small: a 2023 open-label study of 27 adults combined biweekly diamond-tip sessions with hyaluronic acid serums, and a 2009 split-face study in 10 women examined an antioxidant serum used after crystal-free diamond-tip sessions.[2][3]

paras: Microdermabrasion is a non-surgical exfoliation that removes only the outermost dead layer of skin, using an abrasive and suction. It is used for superficial hyperpigmentation, sun damage, fine lines, mild acne and shallow scars, and can help skincare products penetrate better.[1] SilkPeel is a commercial diamond-tip form of this approach, and providers also use the name for the same style of facial.

The first microdermabrasion unit was developed in Italy in 1985 with aluminum oxide crystals; the FDA approved the first machines in 1996 and they reached the US market in 1997. Diamond tips followed in 1999, bristle tips in 2005 and crystal-free vacuum systems in 2012.[1]

In a 2023 open-label, single-center 12-week study, 23 of 27 enrolled adults completed biweekly diamond-tip microdermabrasion paired with serums containing five forms of hyaluronic acid; skin dryness, fine lines, smoothness and radiance improved, effects lasted to week 12, and tolerability was favorable. The study was sponsored by Allergan Aesthetics, and several authors are employees of its parent company.[2]

In a 2009 split-face study, 10 women aged 38 to 52 had six crystal-free diamond-tip sessions; adding a polyphenolic antioxidant serum afterward increased epidermal and papillary dermal thickness and fibroblast density compared with microdermabrasion alone, and skin polyphenol levels rose 32%.[3]

Microdermabrasion has few side effects, mostly temporary dryness and sun sensitivity, with occasional bruising or scratches. Crystal-based systems carry a risk of eye injury and inhalation, which diamond-tip systems avoid.[1] Deeper dermabrasion, a separate surgical procedure, involves bleeding, scarring and pigment change risks and healing over roughly 7 to 30 days.[1]

The identified studies are small and focus on diamond-tip microdermabrasion combined with a serum: a 27-person open-label study with hyaluronic acid serums and a 10-person split-face study with an antioxidant serum.[2][3] Wikipedia's article on the topic notes that its own medical referencing is limited.[1] No studies specific to the SilkPeel brand were identified.
